notes.summary: Percentage means per hundred. SSC asks 1–2 questions in Tier 1 and 1–3 in Tier 2; most are solved in under 45 seconds with fraction equivalents.

concepts.title: Successive change
concepts.body: Two changes a% and b% combine to a + b + ab/100%. Use a negative sign for a decrease.

concepts.title: Price and consumption
concepts.body: Expenditure = Price × Consumption. If the price rises by r%, consumption must fall by r/(100 + r) × 100% to keep expenditure the same.

varieties.name: Percent of a number
varieties.how: Convert the percent to a fraction, then multiply.

example.q: A price rises 20% then falls 10%. Net change?

varieties.name: Price–consumption and more/less than
varieties.how: If A is r% more than B, B is r/(100 + r) × 100 % less than A. The same formula gives the cut in consumption.

example.q: A’s salary is 25% more than B’s. By what percent is B’s salary less than A’s?

tips: For population growth, use successive change or multiply by (1 + r/100) each year.
In election questions, the winning margin is the difference of the two percentages.
traps: A 20% rise followed by a 20% fall is NOT zero change; it is a 4% fall.
“What percent of A is B” uses A as the base: B/A × 100.

formulas.name: Reduce consumption after price rise r%

questions.q: The price of a shirt is increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. The net change is:
The population of a town is 10,000. It increases by 10% every year. What will be the population after 2 years?
The price of sugar rises by 25%. By how much percent must a family reduce its consumption so that its expenditure on sugar remains the same?
In an election between two candidates, one candidate gets 58% of the valid votes and wins by 1120 votes. What is the total number of valid votes?
questions.solution:
Loser gets 100 − 58 = 42%.
Margin = 58% − 42% = 16% of valid votes = 1120.
Valid votes = 1120 × 100/16 = 7000.
